title: Sounding like Billie Holiday, Mildred Bailey and Ella
summary: People say she sounds like Billie, Mildred Bailey or Ella. Dance notes Stanley Dance's point that Humes's early blues records were compared to Mildred before Bailey had recorded.

story.theme_name: Pianists: who played, who influenced whom
story.community_name: Who played piano: the pianists musicians remembered

blocks.x: Yeah, that is nice. Well Mildred was such a funny gal. You must have had a lot of laughs with Mildred, didn't you?
And the pair of you, your voices are-- your styles are not that unlike.
Alot of people think it, don't you?
People have said I sound like Billie Holiday, I sound like Mildred Bailey, and some of them say I sound like Ella. And I said, that's nice.

Well, takes all kinds, all sorts of ears to make the world, doesn't it? That's funny, you know. But Stanley (Dante) mentions in the piece that he wrote that in the very early days, I guess when you made those first blues, back there for Tommy Rockwell, afterwards people said, well that sounded like Mildred.

And Stan made the point that Mildred (Bailey) had never made a record at that point, in those early days. So it's not impossible that some people have a little bit of the same kind of feel as another person, you know?
